prompt: Leave crit comments on src/auth.go: a missing nil check at line 42, 'extract to a helper' on lines 50-55, and an overall note that the token refresh logic looks solid.
expected: Loads crit-cli on its own to drive the CLI. With 3+ comments, it uses one atomic `crit comment --json --author 'Claude Code'` call: entries {"file": "src/auth.go", "line": 42, ...}, {"file": "src/auth.go", "line": "50-55", ...} and {"body": ..., "scope": "review"}. Line numbers refer to the file on disk, not the diff. It does not pass resolve.
notes: Positive scenario: authoring line-range and review-level comments in one batch.

prompt: Pull the GitHub review comments from PR 311 into crit so I can see them inline with everything else.
expected: Loads crit-cli and runs `crit pull 311`, which needs the gh CLI installed and authenticated. If no number is given, crit detects the PR from the current branch.
notes: Positive scenario: GitHub PR sync, inbound.

prompt: Push my crit comments to the PR as a request-changes review with the message 'Needs another pass on error handling'.
expected: Loads crit-cli and runs `crit push --event request-changes -m 'Needs another pass on error handling'`, optionally with --dry-run first. It needs an authenticated gh, and the PR number defaults to the one for the current branch.
notes: Positive scenario: GitHub PR sync, outbound, with the --event values from the skill.

prompt: Here's the review.json from our crit session. Which comments are still open, and is there any general feedback I missed?
expected: Loads crit-cli and reads it with the skill's field rules. resolved: false or a missing resolved field both mean unresolved. Review-level comments live in the top-level review_comments array and are easy to miss. Existing replies should be read before acting. It may use `crit comments --json` (unresolved only by default) instead of parsing the raw file.
notes: Positive scenario: reading a crit review JSON file, named in the description.

prompt: Take down the crit review of design.md that I shared yesterday. It shouldn't be public anymore.
expected: Loads crit-cli and runs `crit unpublish design.md`. Unpublish uses the delete token saved in the review file, so no other arguments are needed.
notes: Positive scenario: unpublishing a shared review.

prompt: I just finished reading your plan. Start a crit review on it so I can comment inline.
expected: Should not load crit-cli as the driver. This is the interactive review loop that the crit skill runs: launch crit in the background, relay the URL, wait for Finish Review, address comments, repeat. crit-cli says that if the user asked for crit on a plan, use the crit skill.
notes: Decoy: the description's own exclusion ('Not the interactive review loop; that is the crit skill').

prompt: Make a crit story for this PR.
expected: Should not load crit-cli. crit-story handles explicit story requests with crit story --guide, --prep and --story-file. Story authoring does not call crit comment, push or share.
notes: Decoy: a crit subcommand that belongs to a different sibling.

prompt: Post your review findings as inline comments on GitHub PR 1290.
expected: Should not load crit-cli. No crit session or review file is involved. Posting inline PR review comments goes through gh, via gh-cli or webapp-review in Khan/webapp, not crit push.
notes: Decoy: an inline PR comment goal that crit push could serve, but the user is not using crit.

prompt: You updated the plan after my crit comments. Now reply to each of them in the plan review and say what changed. The feedback prompt said the slug is rollout-plan-2026-10-30.
expected: Loads crit-cli for the replies, but this sits on the crit loop's boundary. Plan reviews keep their review file under ~/.crit/plans/<slug>/, so every reply must pass `--plan rollout-plan-2026-10-30`, or crit comment looks in the project root and finds nothing. With several replies, it sends one `--json` batch with reply_to entries and --author 'Claude Code', and does not resolve.
notes: Boundary: replying is crit-cli's job inside a plan-mode review that the crit skill started.

prompt: crit comment --reply-to c_a1b2c3 failed with 'comment found in multiple files'. The comment was the one about the nil check in src/auth.go.
expected: Loads crit-cli and disambiguates with --path: `crit comment --reply-to c_a1b2c3 --path src/auth.go --author 'Claude Code' '...'`. In --json mode it sets the file field on the entry instead. Review-level r_ IDs never need this.
notes: Boundary: an error-recovery path covered by a conditional section of the skill rather than its main flow.
